title: Selective dequant avoidance for attention prefill and decode
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Problem statement: During prefill and early decode, the runtime often performs eager dequantization for attention key/value tensors so kernels can run in a single precision path. For many workloads this adds measurable token-level latency and memory bandwidth pressure, especially on INT8/FP8 mixed-precision paths where the dequant epilogue is expensive. We need a targeted approach that avoids unnecessary dequant work for heads/blocks where the native quantized kernel produces acceptable output quality, while still guaranteeing correctness and fallbacks when regressions are detected.

Goals:
- Reduce per-token latency and memory bandwidth during prefill by avoiding full eager dequant for attention when safe.
- Maintain or improve 99th/95th percentile decode latency and tail behavior.
- Keep quality regressions below a defined threshold (per-prompt BLEU/ROUGE/prob-drop or RL-based metric).
- Provide clear telemetry to measure when selective-avoidance is used and its impacts on latency/cost/quality.

Scope: Design and implement a "dequant-avoidance" decision layer in the kernel selection pipeline specifically for attention prefill and early decode. This layer will: (1) consult lightweight heuristics and recent telemetry to decide whether to run a quantized attention kernel directly (skip dequant), (2) allow a fast correctness probe (micro-batch of tokens) to detect unacceptable divergence and trigger fallback to dequant path, (3) expose config knobs for canarying and rollout.

Non-goals: Full model-wide mixed-precision optimizer. This ticket focuses on attention KV paths during prefill/early decode only.
acceptance_criteria: Selective dequant avoidance implemented as a pluggable stage in kernel selection for attention prefill and first 8 decode tokens
End-to-end tests cover at least 3 model families (Llama-like, MPT-like, Falcon-like) and assert quality regression <= defined thresholds
Perf baseline: P95 decode latency reduced >= 6% on INT8 path for sampled workloads; memory bandwidth reduced on prefills by >= 10%
Telemetry dashboard surfaces: avoidance rate, fallback rate, per-model quality delta, and latency/cost delta
Config/rollout flags exist: aggression-level (0-3), probe-sample-size, fallback-backoff, and per-customer opt-out
implementation_plan: Design decision doc and sequence diagram (confluence) describing where the decision layer plugs into kernel selector
Implement lightweight heuristics: headwise variance, token-length heuristics, model-proximity table based on prior telemetry
Add fast probe mechanism: run a 1-2 token quantized attention step and compute fast divergence metric; if below threshold, commit to skip dequant for next N tokens
Integrate with existing kernel abstractions so quantized kernels can accept KV in-place without copy when safe
Add fallback plumbing that triggers zero-copy dequant path and marks telemetry for rollback
Unit tests + microbench harness for kernel latency and memory traces
End-to-end integration tests with runtime scenarios and synthetic traces
Rollout: feature-flagged canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with observable gates
testing_plan: Microkernel benchmarks comparing quantized-attn-skip vs dequant path across sequence lengths [32,128,512] and batch sizes [1,4,16]
Quality regression suite: run canonical prompt set (1000 prompts) for three model families and compute per-prompt logprob delta and token-level mismatch
Stress testing: concurrent prefills and decodes to measure memory bandwidth impact and check for GC/OOM regressions
Chaos tests: force probe mispredictions and assert graceful fallback without corrupting KV cache state
A/B rollout experiments capturing latency/cost/quality on live workloads (internal dev traffic)
rollout_plan: Feature flagged behind runtime.dequant_avoidance with aggression=0 by default
Canary on internal staging region for validated workloads (1 day smoke, 7 day perf/quality collection)
Canary to 10% of hosted traffic with aggressive telemetry retention and automated rollback if fallback_rate > 2% or quality_regression > threshold
Increase to 50% then 100% after 2 stable weeks
Provide per-customer opt-out and per-model forced-disable config
perf_targets: P95 decode latency improvement >= 6% on INT8 prefills compared to current dequantized baseline
Average KV memory write traffic during prefill reduced by >= 10% on target workloads
Fallback rate <= 1% for stable models in canary
No increase in token-level quality failures beyond configured threshold (e.g., median logprob delta < 0.01)
